chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Writing for a girl band and the Savoy Ballroom band with Dizzy
summary: Back in New York, Smith helped Eddie Durham write for a White girl band and led a Savoy Ballroom band with Dizzy Gillespie in 1939.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: What were you doing the rest of the time around New York?

Giggin' wherever we could find one, and hang around and write music. I wrote quite a bit of music for Ida Ray(?) Hubbard(?), a girl White band. Eddie Durham had the job writing for them, and he had me help him out. We'd fix arrangements, send them over there, and those girls would copy them off. The band would rehearse them and get them down, and they'd be gone, go out on the road for awhile. Then we gigged around in their (?) and make up a band, and take them to the Savoy Ballroom, play over there four or five weeks.

Yeah, he was in there. And Gerald(?) Wilson playing trumpet. Him and Dizzy... We didn't have but two trumpet players. And Horsecollar on alto, and I'm on alto. Ike Quebec was on tenor. I forget now who was playing drums. I don't know if it was Sidney Catlett or some other drummer... We had a bunch of them around there to sit in.
